॥ Om. The instruction on liberation for one who is steadfast in the Self. ॥ 1/1/7 ॥

Liberation is not for one who is steadfast in the secondary (non-Self) nature.

It is taught that liberation is for one who is steadfast in the Self, as stated: “Whose Self, having been realized and understood, has entered into this difficult struggle for grasping; he is the Creator of the universe, he is the doer of all; his world is that very world.”

“[Know that] this Self is Brahman.”
“[The Supreme Self is called] Brahman, Paramatman, and Bhagavan.”
“[The Soma] given to Durvasa, which is born of Atma-Isa and Brahman.”
“Consciousness is said to be of two kinds: Jiva (the individual soul) and Atman (the Supreme Self), O Lord. The Jivas are said to be Brahman and others, but the one Atman is Janardana (Vishnu). The term ‘Atman’ is used with respect to the others in a qualified sense. Liberation is declared to arise from the knowledge of that attributeless Atman. But the others, who possess attributes, are not liberated by the knowledge of them. For the Supreme Person is Vishnu, and therefore liberation is remembered to be from Him.”

Thus it is stated in the Padma Purana.
